title: ASPERN evidence test vectors

testKey.says: A test key whose 32-byte Ed25519 seed is published here; it never signs a real report. Real keys: https://aspern.org/api/v1/evidence-keys.

signedBytesRule: Each signature is Ed25519 (RFC 8032, pure, no pre-hash) over the UTF-8 bytes of one canonical JSON text, and that text is also published beside the signature as signedBytes. Manifest signature: the canonical JSON of the manifest object. PDF attestation signature: the canonical JSON of the attestation object. Canonical JSON: object keys sorted by UTF-16 code units (JavaScript's default sort, so "Z" < "a" < "é" and an astral character sorts by its high surrogate), no whitespace, keys whose value is undefined dropped, arrays in order; strings exactly as ECMAScript JSON.stringify writes them (only ", \ and control characters escaped, \b \f \n \r \t in short form and other controls as lowercase \u00xx, a lone surrogate as \udxxx, every other character as itself in UTF-8); numbers as ECMAScript Number::toString writes them (shortest round-trip digits; exponent form below 1e-6 and from 1e21, written e-7 and e+21, never zero-padded; -0 as 0). A manifest and an attestation carry only strings, integers, null and arrays of strings, so no fractional number is ever inside signed bytes. The readings are not re-serialised by anyone: dataDigest is SHA-256 over the readings file exactly as delivered. That file is itself written in the canonical form, but a tool that parses and re-writes it (Python json.dumps writes 1.493231643952987e-05 where the file has 0.00001493231643952987, and 1e-08 where it has 1e-8) produces other bytes and another hash. Hash the bytes, never a re-serialisation. Signature encoding: base64url without padding (RFC 4648 §5). Public key: JWK OKP/Ed25519, x the raw 32 bytes in base64url; its fingerprint is SHA-256 of those 32 bytes in hex.

canonical.name: keys sorted by UTF-16 code units
an astral key sorts by its high surrogate, before U+FFFF
a tiny number keeps the plain form JSON.stringify writes (Python writes 1.493231643952987e-05)
below 1e-6 the exponent is written e-8, not e-08
from 1e21 the exponent carries a plus sign

readingsBytes.name: dataDigest is SHA-256 of the file bytes as delivered; Python json.dumps(sort_keys=True, separators=(',', ':'), ensure_ascii=False) of the same document hashes differently
